title: dr-hands report
description: Hostile report text supplied by the operator. Obtaining or exporting it is outside dr-hands. No report-source executable or credential is accepted.
$comment: The linter bounds encoded input to 1 MiB before parsing, requires UTF-8, rejects duplicate keys, non-JSON constants, and more than 16 nested containers, and never echoes report contents. Schema validation checks structure, not safety. Markdown, HTML-looking text, code snippets, and URLs are data: never locally render, execute, fetch, template, or interpolate them. No attachments, Git bundles, target/image selection, or hooks are accepted. The operator-owned run inventory assigns sensitivity and destinations; source metadata cannot lower sensitivity or choose paths. Reports are copied to a fixed input filename and identified by a digest. A digest is not a safety certificate. A changed report starts a new run, not a source-specific refresh. Every run inventories all images and inputs independently; private reports cannot enter a public-web run. Inference-provider disclosure is accepted and displayed during approval. Public source provenance does not imply public contents.

version.description: Format version. Unsupported versions are rejected rather than guessed.

title.description: Nonempty report title, treated as hostile text rather than a filename or command.

body.description: Nonempty security claim and supporting text. URLs are not fetched locally. Code snippets are not executed by intake.

comments.description: Optional supporting comments; all content remains hostile. The count and total file-size bounds limit parser work, not malicious instructions.

body.description: Nonempty supporting text, never instructions to the local controller.

source.description: Optional provenance only. These strings are not executable names, paths, credentials, fetch instructions, or Run IDs.

name.description: Origin label such as github or hackerone; never selects a plugin.

reference.description: Source-local reference such as a GHSA ID. It does not control resource identity or cause a network request.
